subject: HelixAI POC: traffic intake, warm-up windows, and evaluation cadence
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Park <jordan.park@helixai.com>, Patricia Gomez <patricia.gomez@helixai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Apr 2026 15:23:00 -0700
Subject: HelixAI POC: traffic intake, warm-up windows, and evaluation cadence

Hi Jordan / Patricia —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth for the POC intake. High level ask: we want to capture an initial traffic profile, agree warm-up & burst expectations, and lock the evaluation cadence so our engineers can prepare the runtime config and the eval harness.

1) Workload intake (what we need from you):
   - Baseline RPS, peak RPS and expected burst frequency (examples below).
   - Representative prompt/token-length distribution (mean/median + 95th).
   - Typical concurrency per user/session and any KV-cache patterns (prefill behavior).
   - Sample logs or a small request dump (anonymized) if available.

Attached: helix_poc_workload_matrix.xlsx — please fill the green columns (expected baseline/peaks, token stats, burst durations).

2) Success criteria (proposal):
   - Latency: 95th percentile tail for generation <= 800ms under expected burst pattern.
   - Throughput: sustain peak RPS for 10 minute windows without error-rate > 1%.
   - Correctness: quality smoke-check passing for the initial prompt set (we'll exchange 50 sample prompts).

3) Warm-up & test windows:
   - Recommend a 48-hour warm-up before the official acceptance window so caches and autoscaling stabilize.
   - During warm-up we run two 1-hour probes and one 10-minute stress burst to validate autoscale and cold-start behavior.

4) Ownership & timeline (proposal):
   - Runtime config / kernels / batching: Ben Carter (ben.carter@redwood.com)
   - Billing / capacity commit / quota handshake: Vivek Kulkarni (vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com)
   - Evaluation harness & pass/fail logic: Priyom Das (priyom.das@redwood.com)

Next steps: please complete the attached matrix by Friday 4/10 EOD PST so we can schedule a short technical handoff on Monday (4/13). If anything above looks off, flag it and we’ll adjust.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: helix_poc_workload_matrix.xlsx (xlsx, 120KB)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HelixAI POC: traffic intake, warm-up windows, and evaluation cadence

Kim — quick notes from my side after skimming the call notes / matrix draft:

- For warm-up: 48h is fine, but we should be explicit about KV-cache prefill vs live traffic. If HelixAI can provide a small prefill dataset (IDs + recent contexts), we can pre-populate to avoid artificial cold-starts.
- Burst windows: define both 'short burst' (30–120s) and 'long burst' (5–15 min). We should run one probe for each during warm-up.
- Measurement windows: we'll use rolling 1-minute percentiles and a 10-minute aggregate for throughput stability. That maps well to the 10-minute sustain requirement Kimberly proposed.

I'll prepare a short ops checklist for the Monday handoff (instances, quantization flags, batch/beam defaults).

—Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Park <jordan.park@helixai.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Patricia Gomez <patricia.gomez@helixai.com>, ops@helixai.com
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HelixAI POC: traffic intake, warm-up windows, and evaluation cadence

Kimberly — thanks for the clear notes. Confirming the initial workload numbers so you can slot us into your schedule. See inline: 

- Baseline RPS: 5–10 RPS steady during business hours.
- Peak RPS: short spikes to 80 RPS (typically marketing campaigns), long sustained stress rare but expected up to 25 RPS for ~10 minutes.
- Burst frequency: 2–4 short bursts per day (30–90s), 1 long burst per week (5–15 min).
- Token lengths: mean ~120 tokens, median 95 tokens, 95th ~420 tokens.
- Concurrency: typical concurrency ~4–8 concurrent requests, rare concurrent users up to 30 when marketing triggers.
- Prefill / KV-cache: we can send a prefill file for the most active 500 sessions.

Attached: small sample request dump (anonymized) — forwarding to ops for secure transfer.

Acceptance criteria: we’re aligned on latency targets but would like to add a soft SLA on tail errors: target <1% 5xx during acceptance window. Also request a brief readout after warm-up showing token-level cost delta with any batching/quantization settings you apply.

We can have the filled matrix to you by EOD Monday (4/13) — apologies for the extra day, we’re compiling token histograms. Can we target the handoff on Tue 4/14 at 10:00am PT?

Thanks,
Jordan Park
Head of Integrations
HelixAI

Attachments referenced: helix_sample_requests.json (json, 45KB)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Park <jordan.park@helixai.com>, Patricia Gomez <patricia.gomez@helixai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HelixAI POC: traffic intake, warm-up windows, and evaluation cadence

Jordan / Patricia — perfect, thank you for the detailed numbers. Actioning below and locking dates: 

- Matrix: we’ll accept the EOD Mon 4/13 delivery. Please upload to the Drive link: https://drive.google.com/helix-poc-docs (ops, please set editor perms for jordan.p@helixai).
- Handoff: Tue 4/14 at 10:00am PT — calendar invite sent. Agenda: runtime knobs, prefill ingest, warm-up probes.
- Warm-up: 48-hour warm-up window starting Wed 4/15 09:00 PT; probes as described (one 1h probe, one 10m stress, one long 10m sustain).
- Owners: Ben — runtime & probe orchestration. Vivek — quota / pricing impact if bursts exceed committed capacity. Priyom — evaluation harness + pass/fail automation (Priyom will share the eval checklist before handoff).

Attached: SLO_proposal.pdf (pdf, 85KB) — includes the acceptance gating we discussed.

Jordan, we’ll also include a short token-cost delta table after warm-up so you can see the impact of batching/quantization. If you need an earlier slot for the handoff feel free to suggest alternatives — otherwise we’ll proceed as scheduled.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: slo_proposal.pdf (pdf, 85KB)
